LoloBuy manual order guide: what to enter when a link fails

A manual order should reproduce the seller’s offer accurately enough for a purchasing agent to verify it. The goal is not to fill every box—it is to remove the ambiguities that could change what gets bought.

Editorial note: This independent guide is based on LoloBuy’s current public purchase, order-confirmation, modification, discount and inspection materials, checked on 14 October 2026. Exact form fields and supported sellers can change. Follow the live order screen and do not invent information that the listing does not provide.

When the manual-order route appears

LoloBuy’s current purchase guide describes two submission routes. For supported marketplace pages that can be captured, the buyer can select colour, size and quantity from imported listing information. If the platform instead displays “Fill in A Shopping Agent Order,” the buyer must enter the order information manually before adding it to the cart or buying it.

A manual form is not proof that the product is unavailable, unsafe or unsupported. It means the listing data was not captured into a ready-made option menu. The burden therefore shifts to the information you provide. A vague entry can still be purchased exactly as written, even if it does not match what you had in mind.

The narrow question is: what does a purchasing agent need to identify one exact seller offer without guessing? At minimum, preserve the source, product identity, selected option, quantity, current price, Chinese domestic shipping information and any requirement that can be checked with the seller or at the warehouse.

Start with a stable source record

Paste the direct product link shown by the seller, not a search-results page, shortened redirect, social post or screenshot-only reference. Open the link in a private browser window before submitting it. If the page requires your personal login, loads a different product outside your session or has already been removed, the agent may not see the same offer.

Save a dated screenshot or PDF of the listing for your own records. Capture the title, seller name, main image, selected option, price, domestic delivery information and any promotion you expect to use. This private evidence should not replace the live link, but it helps you explain a change if the seller edits the page after submission.

Use a short, descriptive product name rather than copying a page full of promotional text. Include the item type and the detail that separates it from similar products: “navy zip hoodie, fleece-lined version” is more useful than “new autumn bestseller.” Do not add a brand, material or specification that the seller does not state. For made-to-order text, artwork or dimensions, use the separate customized product guide to document approval points before payment.

Translate the option without changing it

Manual ordering is most error-prone when one option label combines colour, size, version, bundle and quantity. Preserve the seller’s original option wording, then add a plain-English explanation beside it. The original text gives the agent something exact to match; your explanation shows how you interpreted it.

For clothing, connect the chosen size to the seller’s own chart rather than a generic US or European conversion. For shoes, distinguish foot length from insole length. For electronics and accessories, record model, connector, voltage, plug, length or left/right orientation where the listing supplies it. The size and variant checklist gives a detailed method for separating these choices.

If two seller options look identical or the translation is uncertain, stop before payment. Put one focused question in the order enquiry instead of choosing the option that seems most likely. “Does option 02 include the charger and EU plug?” can be checked. “Please make sure it is the good one” cannot.

Define quantity and set contents separately

Quantity should mean the number of complete seller units you want. It should not be used to repair an unclear bundle. A listing might offer one pair, one piece, a two-piece set, a replacement component or a wholesale pack under similar photographs. Record both the number of units and what one unit is supposed to contain.

For example: “Quantity: 2 seller units. Each unit: one strap only; no watch.” If a listing photo shows props or accessories that are not mentioned in the selected option, do not include them in your expectation. Ask the seller before ordering if missing contents would make you cancel.

Record price, domestic shipping and promotions honestly

LoloBuy’s public workflow says the first payment covers the item and Chinese domestic delivery. Use the price attached to the exact selected option, not the lowest headline price displayed for another size, deposit or accessory. Keep product price and domestic shipping separate so an agent can see what needs verification.

The official discount FAQ says a buyer can modify the product price or shipping amount when a seller offers a discount or free domestic shipping and describe the offer in remarks. The shopping agent then verifies it with the seller. That does not make every coupon transferable or guarantee that a time-limited promotion will still be active when the order is placed.

Write the promotion in verifiable terms: seller price before discount, expected discounted price, free-shipping condition, promotion name or seller message, and the date you observed it. Do not reduce the entered price without explaining why. If the seller will not confirm the offer, be prepared to accept the live amount, add funds or cancel under the current order rules.

Use remarks for decisions, not decoration

A strong remark tells the agent what must be confirmed before purchase and what visible detail should later match. Keep it short. Separate requirements from preferences and avoid asking the warehouse to prove things outside its inspection scope.

A practical remark might read: “Buy only the navy, fleece-lined XL option shown in seller image 4. Confirm that the selected price is for one complete hoodie, not a deposit. If XL is unavailable, do not substitute. At warehouse, size tag and visible colour must match.”

LoloBuy’s inspection scope covers visible information such as style, quantity, colour, size and model. It excludes professional judgments about electronics, authenticity, function and quality, and it does not open many sealed products. A manual note cannot expand that scope. If your decision depends on internal components, performance or authenticity, the listing and seller must provide the answer before purchase.

Review the complete order before payment

Compare the manual entry with the source page one line at a time:

Source: Does the link open the exact product for someone who is not logged into your seller account?

Identity: Do the title, seller and main image describe the same listing?

Option: Are colour, size, version, model and included parts explicit?

Quantity: Is the number of seller units separate from the contents of each unit?

Money: Does the selected-option price match the page, and is domestic shipping recorded separately?

Stop condition: Have you said what the agent should do if the option, promotion or stock cannot be confirmed?

Destination and services: Have you selected the intended destination country and only the value-added services currently offered and actually needed?

What happens if information is unclear

LoloBuy says a shopping-agent order may enter “Pending for Confirmation” when item information needs to be verified again. Follow the instruction shown on the order and answer the specific uncertainty. Before warehouse arrival, confirmation is handled through the shopping-agent order area; later warehouse-stage questions can appear in the warehouse area.

Do not ignore a confirmation request because the seller page still looks correct to you. The agent may be seeing a stock issue, price difference, ambiguous option or seller response that is not visible on the public page. Reply with the saved source evidence and a clear accept, replace, cancel or ask decision.

The modification FAQ also draws an important line: if the seller has not dispatched, LoloBuy can try to negotiate a change. After seller dispatch, modification generally cannot be negotiated at that stage. A buyer who still wants a different option may need to wait for warehouse arrival, request a return and submit a new order, with resulting domestic delivery or return costs. This is why a two-minute manual-entry review matters.

A reusable manual-order note

Product: plain product name and direct seller link
Seller: shop name shown on the source page
Selected option: original seller wording plus plain-English meaning
Quantity: number of seller units and contents per unit
Price: exact selected-option price
Domestic shipping: displayed amount or documented free-shipping condition
Promotion: seller-confirmable terms and observation date
Must confirm before purchase: one or two questions that change the decision
Do not substitute: unavailable option, higher price or different version that requires approval
Visible warehouse check: tag, colour, model or component count within ordinary inspection limits

Conclusion: make the order reproducible

The best LoloBuy manual order is one another person can reproduce without reading your mind. Keep the seller link, preserve the original option label, define the unit and contents, separate item price from domestic shipping, document promotions and write a clear stop condition. Then respond quickly if the order moves to Pending for Confirmation.

Manual entry cannot repair an unreliable seller page or turn an unobservable claim into warehouse evidence. When the listing is too ambiguous to describe precisely, the safer decision is to ask, find a clearer listing or not order. To research products before creating the record, open FindSpreadsheet →
